name: flash-fisheye-y2k
keep: KEEP — the making of the image, copy exactly:

· MEDIUM: a hyper-sharp editorial photograph shot with HARD DIRECT ON-CAMERA FLASH through an ultra-wide FISHEYE lens, from an extreme low angle looking up. Wet specular highlights, glossy skin, crushed shadow, slightly over-sharpened.
· LENS: strong fisheye barrel distortion — straight structural lines bow into curves, the subject looms large and warped toward the glass while the edges stretch and bend away.
· GROUND: shot from beneath a bright industrial steel structure — riveted girders and beams overhead, a metal railing and glittering water behind, with a wedge of pale blue sky at the frame edge.
· LIGHT: harsh close flash blast in the foreground over warm ambient daylight, sun-baked golden bounce off metal, blown-out highlights.
· PALETTE: hot saturated candy tones — tangerine orange, spring green and fire-engine red — over a warm ochre-yellow ground and a slice of sky blue.
· TEXTURE: fine analog film grain plus faint print noise across the whole frame, punchy over-saturated contrast.
· MOOD: chaotic, playful, hyper-real Y2K street-fashion energy.
· No readable text, no letters, no numerals, no logo, no watermark anywhere.
